subject: Week 1: Here we go. Genesis to Leviticus.
body:
Good morning.

Welcome to week one. This week you read creation, the flood, Abraham, Joseph, and the exodus from Egypt, and you will end at the door of Leviticus. About thirteen chapters a day. Steady, not rushed.

Do not worry about understanding every detail. Just read, and let the story pull you in. Your dashboard has each day's chapters, and I am reading right alongside you.

Heather

subject: Week 2: The wilderness years
body:
Good morning.

This week is Leviticus, Numbers, and most of Deuteronomy. I will be honest: this is the stretch where people quit. All those laws and lists are God teaching freed slaves how to live near a holy God.

If you fall behind a day, do not go back. Just read today's reading. No guilt. Showing up beats catching up.

Heather

subject: Week 3: Into the land, and a king after God's heart
body:
Good morning.

Big week. Moses says goodbye, Joshua crosses the Jordan, the judges spiral, Ruth stays, and Samuel anoints David. You will watch Israel go from wanderers to a kingdom in seven days.

Watch for the pattern: every time the people forget God, things fall apart. Every time they cry out, He answers.

Heather

subject: Week 4: Kings, and the cost of drifting
body:
Good morning.

David at his best and worst this week, then Solomon, the temple, and a kingdom that tears in two. Elijah stands on Carmel and hides in a cave in the same chapter of his life.

The Bible does not clean anybody up, and that is exactly why you can trust it.

Heather

subject: Week 5: Exile, return, and a man named Job
body:
Good morning.

This week the kingdoms fall, the exiles come home to rebuild, Esther risks everything, and then you meet Job, a man who lost it all and refused to let go of God.

Some of this week is heavy. Read it anyway. The hard books hold the deepest hope.

Heather

subject: Week 6: Job ends. The songs begin.
body:
Good morning.

God finally answers Job this week, and He does not explain Himself. He shows Himself. Then you step into the Psalms, the Bible's songbook: praise, anger, fear, and trust, sometimes all in one song.

Read a few of them out loud. They were written to be prayed.

Heather

subject: Week 7: Psalms into Proverbs
body:
Good morning.

You finish the psalms this week and walk into Proverbs. From songs that carry your heart to one-liners that run your week: money, words, anger, friendship.

Halfway is close. You have read more of the Bible in six weeks than most people read in years. Keep going.

Heather

subject: Week 8: Wisdom, love, and the Holy One
body:
Good morning.

Proverbs wraps up, Ecclesiastes tells the truth about chasing everything but God, Song of Solomon celebrates love, and then Isaiah lifts your eyes. Watch for chapter 53 next week coming into view: the servant who was pierced for us.

For unto us a child is born. It is all pointing somewhere.

Heather

subject: Week 9: The weeping prophet and the watchman
body:
Good morning.

Isaiah finishes, and then Jeremiah preaches to a nation that will not listen, and weeps over it in Lamentations. Ezekiel sees visions by the river of Babylon.

Great is His faithfulness. His mercies are new every morning. That line was written in the rubble. It still holds.

Heather

subject: Week 10: Dry bones and the minor prophets
body:
Good morning.

Ezekiel promises a new heart, Daniel stands tall in Babylon, and then you sprint through the twelve minor prophets: Hosea's relentless love, Jonah's second chance, Micah's simple requirement. Do justice. Love mercy. Walk humbly.

The Old Testament ends this week and next with a promise, then four hundred years of silence.

Heather

subject: Week 11: He arrives
body:
Good morning.

This is the week everything has been leaning toward. Malachi's last word, silence, and then Matthew: the genealogy that carries every story you have read straight to a manger.

You will read Matthew, Mark, Luke, and into John this week. Four witnesses. One Jesus.

Heather

subject: Week 12: The church explodes
body:
Good morning.

John finishes, the Spirit falls at Pentecost, and the gospel starts running across the map through shipwrecks and prison cells. Then Paul's letters begin: Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, and more.

Nothing can separate us from the love of God. Two more weeks of reading, and one of them is already almost done.

Heather

subject: Week 13: You are going to finish this
body:
Good morning.

The final week. The last letters, the faith hall of fame in Hebrews 11, and then Revelation: no more tears, no more death, He makes all things new.

The story that started in a garden ends in a city. You read the whole Bible in ninety days. I am so proud of you. Finish strong, then go get your certificate.

Heather
